title: Endpoint Surface Safety Net: Behavioral PRD and Canary Slice Launch Checklist
creator: Maya Patel
description: This PRD defines a safety-net layer and staged canary strategy for the hosted inference surface (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). The goal is to reduce customer-visible regressions during launches and model/infra rollouts by codifying behavioral contracts, telemetry gates, and automated fallback policies. The document bundles product requirements, acceptance criteria, and an operational launch checklist for canary slices and progressive rollout of endpoint changes.
problem_statement: Recent launches mixing model upgrades and infra tuning have produced subtle quality regressions and cost/latency surprises for a subset of heavy users. We need a product-level safety net that enforces behavioral SLAs per lane, orchestrates safe canary slices, and provides clear acceptance gates so we can ship faster with lower regression risk.
out_of_scope: Major API surface redesigns (e.g., new protocols)
End-to-end retraining or model architecture research
goals: Detect behavioral regressions early with per-lane signal sets
Provide automated fallback and graded degradations to preserve availability
Define clear canary slice sizes and traffic ramp rules for hosted endpoints
Ensure acceptance gates are observable and actionable from Console
user_stories: As a PM, I want automated canary slices so I can validate model + infra changes on low-risk traffic before full rollouts.
As an SRE, I want telemetry gates that stop a rollout if latency or quality slips so we avoid customer-impacting degradations.
As a developer, I want a predictable fallback policy (model variant -> quantized variant -> degrade mode) so code paths behave consistently under load.
acceptance_criteria: Functional: Canary routing supports arbitrary slice predicates (by account, region, or header) and can be configured via Console and API.
Quality: For chat/completions, top-level semantic similarity to baseline measured by evaluation set must be within 2% of baseline across 5k sampling queries for canary slice.
Embedding: Average pairwise cosine similarity drift less than 0.5% on the canonical anchor set for canary traffic.
Rerank: NDCG@10 delta <= 0.01 compared to baseline on canary evaluation traffic.
Latency: p95 request latency for canary slice must not exceed baseline p95 by more than 20ms for gen endpoints and 10ms for embedding endpoints.
Error budget: No more than 0.5% increase in 5xx rate on canary slice relative to historical baseline.
Rollout gate: Automated rollback triggers implemented for each gate (metrics, quality, errors) with configurable thresholds and alerting.
Observability: Console displays slice-level cost breakdown, latency histogram, quality regression flag, and rollout status.
Docs: Public API docs updated with canary routing knobs and examples before release.
Security: Security review signed-off and KMS-backed keys verified for telemetry export pipelines.
metrics_and_slos: Canary p50/p95 latency per endpoint and model variant
Evaluation-Driven Quality Score (semantic sim for gen, NDCG for rerank, cosine drift for embeddings)
Cost per 1k tokens or 1k embeddings for canary vs baseline
rollout_checklist: Define canary slice predicates (accounts, cohorts, regions) and register in Console
Create evaluation query sets covering common failure modes for each endpoint
Wire automated gates to monitoring (metrics -> gating lambda) with thresholds from acceptance_criteria
Implement fallback chains and confirm model variant compatibility for fallbacks
Run synthetic traffic storm to validate autoscaling and batching behaviors under canary load
Perform internal dogfood on 3 pilot accounts for 48 hours
Run manual QA on 200 sampled canary responses for each endpoint type
Prepare runbook with rollback steps and on-call assignments
Enable rollout with 1% traffic slice, monitor 6 hours, then 5% then 20% following gate checks
Update public changelog and customer communications for tenant-affecting changes
runbook_high_level: If quality gate trips: pause rollout, start detailed analysis using evaluation shard, consider model revert or parameter tweak.
If latency gate trips: reduce concurrency, switch to lower-cost model variant, or enable degrade mode (reduce response length or disable streaming).
If error gate trips: revert to last stable deployment and open incident with SRE and ModelOps.
open_questions: What is the canonical evaluation set ownership per endpoint? (PM vs Research)
How long should we run canary at each ramp step for long-tail metric stability?
Is there a safe default fallback chain for private deployments where model variants may be restricted?
Should customer-visible notifications be automatic or gated by account managers?
decisions_log: 2025-07-30: Use 1%, 5%, 20% ramp model with 6-hour stability window per step (decision by PM + SRE)
2025-07-31: Quality gate thresholds set to conservative defaults: 2% gen similarity drift, 0.5% embedding cosine drift (decision by PM + Research)
2025-08-01: Canary predicates include account-id hashing + region; header-based slice reserved for internal tests only (decision by Eng)
2025-08-03: Security review required for telemetry exports to third-party endpoints (decision by Security)
2025-08-04: Require Console view to surface cost delta for canaries before ramping beyond 5% (decision by PM)

implementation_notes: Eng deliverables: canary router, gating lambda, fallback orchestration, canary telemetry tags.
Design deliverables: Console slice UI, canary status indicators, integrated changelog snippet.
Research deliverables: canonical eval sets + automated sampling harness for canary traffic.
post_launch_checks: 72-hour post-rollout QA sweep: sample 1k responses per endpoint from production and validate against acceptance thresholds
30-day regression watch: weekly quality and cost report to PM and SRE owners
Customer feedback channel opened for pilot accounts and triage SLA defined
